fix(build): fall back to copying assets when `outDir` is on another filesystem
withastro/astro
#18542Oct 29

Changes

  • Static builds fail with EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted when outDir is outside the project and on a different filesystem, and a prerendered page emits an asset (for example an image rendered with <Image>). With outDir outside the working directory, prerender output is written to .astro/.prerender/ in the working directory (see getOutDirWithinCwd), and ssrMoveAssets moves those assets into outDir with fs.promises.rename, which cannot cross filesystems. This has failed since 6.0.0, when the prerender asset move was added.
  • Adds a moveFile() helper to core/fs that renames the file and, when rename fails with EXDEV, copies it and removes the source. Other errors are rethrown.
  • Uses moveFile() for both moves in ssrMoveAssets. Only the prerender move is known to cross filesystems; the SSR-assets move is switched too for consistency.
  • Adds a patch changeset.

This overlaps with two open PRs, so whichever merges second will need a small rebase:

  • #18480 changes the same two call sites. Its moveOrCopyAsset helper uses rename for files other than .wasm, which should call moveFile once both land.
  • #18503 changes the same import line in static-build.ts and adds a helper at the same place in core/fs/index.ts.

Testing

Added test/units/fs/move-file.test.ts, which covers a plain move, the EXDEV fallback (with fs.promises.rename stubbed to fail as it does across devices, since CI has no second filesystem), and rethrowing other errors.

Reproduction, checked by hand against this branch:

  1. npm create astro@latest -- --template minimal
  2. Add src/assets/pic.png and render it from src/pages/index.astro: 
    ---
import { Image } from 'astro:assets';
import pic from '../assets/pic.png';
---
<html lang="en"><body><Image src={pic} alt="" /></body></html>
  3. astro build --outDir <a directory on another filesystem>
Astro outDir on the same filesystem outDir on another filesystem
5.18.2 builds builds
6.0.0 builds fails with EXDEV
7.4.4 builds fails with EXDEV
this branch builds builds

With this branch, the output on the other filesystem is byte-identical to the output of a same-filesystem build.

Docs

No docs needed: this is an internal fix with no change to configuration or documented behavior.

Fix autogenerated sidebar omitting directories named like Object.prototype properties
withastro/starlight
#4309Oct 28

Description

  • Closes #4306
  • Autogenerated sidebar groups omitted directories whose names match Object.prototype properties (e.g. constructor, toString, hasOwnProperty). makeDir() created directory nodes as plain {} objects, so in treeify(), currentNode[part] ||= makeDir(...) resolved to the inherited property (truthy) and never created the directory. Pages inside were dropped from the tree, which also broke current-page highlighting and prev/next links.
  • Directory nodes are now created with Object.create(null), so only real directory entries exist on them.
  • Added a regression test covering constructor, toString, and hasOwnProperty directories (fails without the fix), plus a patch changeset.
Fix `size-limit` CI job
withastro/starlight
#4308Oct 28

Description

This PR fixes an issue due to the switch to pnpm 12 in #4276.

In the size-limit job, we use the andresz1/size-limit action which by default runs npx size-limit --json.

Since then, we now uses the devEngines.packageManager field in package.json to list pnpm as the package manager, so npm refuses to run with a EBADDEVENGINES error.

As documented, to fix the issue, we customize the script to use pnpm 🤞

This was not an issue before as npm seems to only care about devEngines.packageManager and not packageManager.

Note that the size-limit-basic job is not impacted as we run pnpm size without the action.

fix(content): let unused render() tree-shake out of server bundles
withastro/astro
#18536Oct 28

Changes

  • astro:content builds render with a factory call since #17818 (7.3.0): export const render = createRenderEntry({ logger }). The bundler keeps unannotated calls, so renderEntry stays in every server bundle that imports astro:content. Its dynamic import('astro:content-module-imports') stays with it. That's the map that lazily imports every renderable entry.
  • As a result, when on-demand routes only read collection data (getCollection(), getEntry()) and never call render(), every entry rendered by prerendered pages is still compiled into the server output. In 7.2, renderEntry was a plain exported function and was tree-shaken.
  • This marks the factory call /* @__PURE__ */, so an unused render is dropped again. Bundles that do use render() keep it, so runtime behavior is unchanged.

Real-world impact: on a Vercel site with ~200 MDX posts in 11 locales and a few on-demand routes (/blog listing, /compare/*), the _render function went from 50 MB (7.2.10) to 389 MB (7.3.0 through 7.4.2). Vercel rejects that: "exceeds the maximum uncompressed size limit of 250mb". With this change it's back to 49 MB, and all of the site's on-demand routes still render.

Bisected on that site: 7.2.10 builds a 49 MB function, while 7.3.1, 7.3.4, 7.3.8, 7.4.0 and 7.4.2 build 389–390 MB. Walking the server environment's module graph points to this chain:

on-demand page → astro:content → content/runtime.js (renderEntry)
  → import('astro:content-module-imports') → import(<every entry>.mdx?astroPropagatedAssets)

Testing

  • Added content-render-tree-shaking.test.ts with a fixture that has two MDX entries, a prerendered page that renders them with render(), and an on-demand page that only calls getCollection(). The test asserts that no server chunk contains an entry's compiled body, and that both pages render. The fixture uses retainBody: false, so the marker can only reach the server output through a compiled entry module and not through the data store.
    • Without the change, it fails: dist/server/chunks/first_*.mjs contains the entry.
    • With the change, it passes.
  • test/content*.test.ts, test/ssr-prerender*.test.ts, test/server-islands.test.ts, test/csp-server-islands.test.ts and test/live-*.test.ts all pass (80/80).

Docs

No docs needed: this is a bundle-size fix with no API or behavior change.

Prevent memory cache from storing empty 404/500 responses that would be rerouted to error pages
withastro/astro
#18522Oct 27

Changes

  • Cached 404/500 responses with a null body are no longer stored in the memory provider. Previously, serializeResponse() converted the null body to an empty ArrayBuffer, so cache hits returned an empty response body instead of the rendered error page (which the router could only produce when response.body === null).
  • Adds an isErrorPageReroute() guard in core/cache/memory-provider.ts that skips caching (and deletes any stale SWR entry) when the response has a reroutable status (404 or 500) and a null body. One trade-off: endpoints that return an empty 404/500 with skipErrorReroute will also bypass the cache, though the response they send is still correct.

Testing

  • New unit tests in packages/astro/test/units/cache/memory-provider.test.ts covering both the initial-request path and the SWR revalidation path for empty 404 and 500 responses, asserting they are not stored and that stale entries are evicted.

Docs

  • No docs update needed; this is a bug fix restoring the already-documented behavior of the memory cache provider.

Closes #18456

undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unhandled error on excessive content-encodings

CVE-2026-109869 / GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

More information

Details

Impact

undici's fetch() crashes the Node.js process when a malicious server returns a response with more than five content codings and closes the connection before sending the body. undici rejects such responses (a content-encoding limit), but it created the internal response stream before that check and returned without attaching an error listener or aborting the request. The early close then surfaces a content-length mismatch on that orphaned internal stream, which Node.js treats as an unhandled error and terminates the process. A remote, unauthenticated server can trigger this with a single response, even when the application correctly catches the fetch() rejection. undici 6.x, 7.x, and 8.x are affected.

Patches

Upgrade to 6.29.1, 7.30.1, or 8.12.2. undici now validates the content-encoding chain before creating the internal body stream and aborts the response when the limit is exceeded, so no error can surface on an orphaned stream.

Workarounds

None.

Severity

  • CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
  • Vector String: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

undici vulnerable to Subresource Integrity bypass via non-lowercase algorithm tokens

CVE-2026-109841 / GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472

More information

Details

Impact

undici's fetch() verifies Subresource Integrity (SRI) metadata by looking up the algorithm token in a lowercase-only set, but the SRI specification defines a valid token by its ASCII-lowercase form. A correct but non-lowercase token such as SHA256-... or Sha256-... is therefore treated as unknown and skipped. When no recognized algorithm remains, undici treats the integrity list as empty and accepts the response, so a server that returns a body different from the pinned digest passes the check.

An application that pins a response with a valid uppercase or mixed-case SRI token receives attacker-controlled bytes with no integrity error. The attacker needs only to control the response body, not the application's integrity metadata. The issue affects response integrity only. The regression was introduced in undici 7.15.0; releases 7.14.0 and earlier lowercase the token and are not affected.

Patches

Upgrade to 7.30.1 or 8.12.2. undici now normalizes the algorithm token to ASCII lowercase before validating it and before selecting the strongest algorithm, so case variants of SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 are verified correctly.

Workarounds

Use lowercase algorithm tokens (sha256, sha384, sha512) in integrity metadata.

undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unbounded memory in the EventSource parser

CVE-2026-109924 / GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

More information

Details

Impact

undici's EventSource client can be driven to exhaust process memory by a malicious or compromised Server-Sent Events peer. By sending millions of tiny completed data: fields with no blank event separator, or a single unfinished line split across many chunks, the parser retains a growing amount of per-field and per-chunk state. The byte-based maxEventSize and maxResponseSize limits do not bound that retained state, and maxResponseSize is enforced on the compressed body before decompression, so a small compressed response can expand into enough retained memory to terminate the process. The application only needs to maintain an EventSource connection to an untrusted peer, which controls only the response. Availability is the only impact.

Patches

Upgrade to 6.29.1, 7.30.1, or 8.12.2, which bound the retained EventSource parser state (the number of data fields and buffered chunks, the unfinished-line length, and per-field byte totals) independently of the byte limits.

Workarounds

None.

undici WebSocket client vulnerable to Denial of Service via failed HTTP/2 handshake

CVE-2026-109855 / GHSA-qq8j-7v2v-3rwp

More information

Details

Impact

undici's experimental WebSocket client (enabled by default via allowH2: true) crashes the Node.js process when it connects to a malicious server over HTTP/2. If the server answers the WebSocket upgrade with a response that fails handshake validation, undici aborts the request, but the abort is a no-op because the request is already marked completed, so the underlying ClientHttp2Stream is left open with no error listener. When the server then destroys the connection, the orphaned stream emits an unhandled error and the process exits. A remote, unauthenticated server can therefore deny service to any client that opens a WebSocket to it over HTTP/2. undici 8.11.0 and 8.11.1 are affected; the regression was introduced in 8.11.0.

Patches

Upgrade to 8.11.2.

Workarounds

Set allowH2: false to disable HTTP/2 for WebSocket connections, or avoid opening WebSocket connections to untrusted servers, until upgrading.

Severity

  • CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
  • Vector String: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

undici WebSocket client vulnerable to Denial of Service via unbounded automatic PONG buffering

CVE-2026-109932 / GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6

More information

Details

Impact

undici's WebSocket client (including Node.js's bundled globalThis.WebSocket) can be driven to exhaust process memory by a malicious or compromised WebSocket server. For every PING frame received, the receiver automatically writes a PONG response to the socket and ignores the false return value from socket.write(), which is a backpressure signal, so a server that streams small PING frames while never reading the client's PONGs makes the outbound write queue and heap grow without bound until the Node.js process runs out of memory and terminates. The attack is remote and unauthenticated, needs only a normal WebSocket connection, and is asymmetric: small inbound PINGs produce a much larger retained outbound queue. Availability is the only impact. undici 5.x, 6.x, 7.x, and 8.x are affected; the WebSocket client was introduced in 5.15.0.

Patches

Upgrade to 6.29.1, 7.30.1, or 8.12.2, which pause WebSocket frame parsing when the automatic PONG response hits socket backpressure and resume on drain, bounding the outbound queue.

Workarounds

None.

Severity

  • CVSS Score: 5.9 / 10 (Medium)
  • Vector String: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 / GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

More information

Details

Impact

undici crashes the client process when a TLS 1.2 server renegotiates after the connection is established and presents a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname does not match the requested host. Node.js re-runs hostname verification on the renegotiated handshake and destroys the socket with ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID. undici's established socket error handler asserted that this error code could never occur, so the peer-controlled error became an uncaught AssertionError that terminates the Node.js process. Both the HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 paths are affected.

A malicious or compromised HTTPS endpoint reached through undici or the global fetch() can crash the client with a single server-initiated renegotiation, taking down all in-flight requests and background work in the process. Only TLS 1.2 is affected, because TLS 1.3 does not support renegotiation. Exploitation does not require a CA compromise: the attacker controls the endpoint and can present two ordinary valid certificates, the first matching the requested URL and the second intentionally not matching it.

Patches

Upgrade to undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1, or 8.12.2.

Workarounds

Restrict outbound connections to TLS 1.3, for example by setting connect: { minVersion: 'TLSv1.3', maxVersion: 'TLSv1.3' } on the client or agent, so that renegotiation cannot occur, when the target endpoints support TLS 1.3.

Severity

  • CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
  • Vector String: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

undici vulnerable to TLS certificate validation bypass via dropped tls options in Agent

CVE-2026-109383 / GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

More information

Details

Impact

undici's Agent passes its constructor options through a JSON-based deep clone (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))) before forwarding them to each per-origin Pool. JSON cannot represent functions, so a caller-supplied tls option containing a checkServerIdentity callback is silently dropped before it reaches the TLS layer. As a result, a TLS peer whose certificate a custom checkServerIdentity was written to reject, but which passes Node's default hostname and chain checks, is silently accepted when the request is made through Agent. Because Agent is the default dispatcher behind request, fetch, and setGlobalDispatcher, this is the path most applications use. EnvHttpProxyAgent is also affected on its direct and NO_PROXY routes, which delegate to an internal Agent.

Only applications that pass a function-valued tls option (such as a custom checkServerIdentity for certificate or public-key pinning) are affected. Passing the same options through connect is not affected. This is the Agent counterpart of the BalancedPool certificate validation bypass fixed in CVE-2026-84961.

Patches

Upgrade to undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1, or 8.12.2. Agent now preserves the tls option outside the JSON clone, so custom TLS verification callbacks are forwarded to each origin unchanged.

Workarounds

Pass the TLS options through connect instead of tls. For proxied EnvHttpProxyAgent destinations, use requestTls / proxyTls.

Severity

  • CVSS Score: 7.4 / 10 (High)
  • Vector String: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

undici vulnerable to cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure via cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 / GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

More information

Details

Impact

When an originless Agent composes the redirect and cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()) with a shared cache (type: 'shared'), the cache builds its key from the original request URL before the redirect handler changes the origin. The response produced after a redirect is then stored under the original key, even when the redirect crossed to a different origin.

An attacker who controls the target of a redirect from a trusted URL can have their response cached under that trusted URL. A later caller requesting the trusted URL receives the attacker's body from the shared cache without either origin being contacted, allowing persistent cache poisoning. The same key confusion also discloses private data: when an authenticated request returns a private, no-store redirect to a user-specific resource, the final response is stored under the original URL and can be served to a later unauthenticated caller.

The cache interceptor was introduced in undici 7.0.0, and all 7.x and 8.x releases before the patched versions are affected. Applications are affected only when an originless Agent, a shared MemoryCacheStore or SqliteCacheStore, and the composition compose(redirect(), cache()) are all used. Origin-bound Client and Pool dispatchers, and the reverse composition compose(cache(), redirect()), are not affected.

Patches

Upgrade to 7.30.1 or 8.12.2. Before storing a response, undici now verifies that the origin that produced it still matches the cache key, and preserves each redirect hop's cache-control policy, so cross-origin redirect responses and responses behind a no-store or private hop are no longer cached under the original key.

Workarounds

Compose the interceptors as compose(cache(), redirect()), use per-origin dispatchers and cache stores, or disable shared caching on redirect-capable requests.

Severity

  • CVSS Score: 7.4 / 10 (High)
  • Vector String: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unhandled exception in the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 / GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

More information

Details

Impact

undici's decompress interceptor forwards decompressed response data to the downstream handler from zlib stream event callbacks without catching exceptions those callbacks may throw. undici's engine converts a synchronous throw from a downstream handler into a per-request failure, but that protection is not in place when the throw happens asynchronously from a zlib callback. As a result, a downstream handler that throws by design, for example the built-in dump interceptor which throws when a response exceeds its maxSize, escapes as an uncaught exception and terminates the Node.js process.

A malicious or compromised HTTP server can crash any client that composes the decompress interceptor with dump (or another response handler that throws), by returning a small compressed body that decompresses to more than the configured limit. The compressed bytes on the wire are tiny, so only the decompressed size matters. If the application keeps the process alive with a global uncaught-exception handler, the affected request instead hangs until the body timeout.

Patches

Upgrade to undici 7.30.1 or 8.12.2.

Workarounds

Avoid composing the decompress interceptor with a response handler that throws during response processing (such as dump with a maxSize) until upgrading.

Severity

  • CVSS Score: 5.9 / 10 (Medium)
  • Vector String: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Release Notes

nodejs/undici (undici)

v8.12.2

Compare Source

Security fixes

High severity
Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 · GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

When an originless Agent combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()), a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity
Denial of service through the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 · GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

An exception thrown by a downstream response handler from an asynchronous decompression callback could escape as an uncaught exception. A server could trigger this when decompress was composed with a handler such as dump with a size limit. This release converts downstream handler exceptions into per-request errors.

Subresource Integrity bypass with non-lowercase algorithm tokens

CVE-2026-109841 · GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472

fetch() treated valid mixed-case or uppercase SRI algorithm tokens, such as SHA256, as unknown and could accept a response whose body did not match the configured digest. This release normalizes algorithm tokens before validation and digest selection.

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

CVE-2026-109932 · GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6

A malicious WebSocket server could exhaust process memory by flooding the client with PING frames while not reading the automatic PONG responses. undici previously ignored socket backpressure and allowed the outbound queue to grow without bound. This release pauses frame parsing when PONG writes encounter backpressure and resumes after the socket drains.

fix(transitions): silence ready rejection before skipTransition in ClientRouter
withastro/astro
#18517Oct 26

Fixes #18516.

When a second navigation starts before the previous view transition is ready, abortAndRecreateMostRecentTransition() calls skipTransition() on the pending transition. skipTransition() does not throw — it rejects viewTransition.ready with an AbortError. The try/catch around the call never covers that rejection, so it surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection in the browser console and fires any global unhandledrejection listener (error trackers, test runners).

The fix adds .catch(() => {}) on viewTransition.ready immediately before skipTransition(). This registers a handler for the rejection before it is created, silencing it. The stale comment ("might throw AbortError DOMException") is replaced with one that describes the actual behaviour.

The second navigation still completes normally — the only observable change is that the AbortError is no longer unhandled.

fix(csp): include hashes inserted by body components in the CSP meta tag for non-streaming renders
withastro/astro
#18512Oct 25

Changes

Fixes #18479.

Problem

When a component inside <body> calls Astro.csp.insertScriptHash(), its hash can be missing from the CSP <meta> tag because the tag is rendered before the component runs.

Layouts with <slot name="head" /> previously avoided this issue because asynchronous slot rendering buffered the body before the head was flushed. #17857 allowed synchronous slots to stay synchronous

Fix

For non-streaming renders, this PR delays generating the CSP <meta> tag until the whole page has rendered:

  1. The head writes a placeholder comment where the CSP <meta> tag belongs.
  2. After rendering completes, renderPage replaces the placeholder with the final tag, including hashes registered by body components.

This builds moves the replacement logic to renderPage so the fix covers both .astro and MDX pages.

Scope

This fix covers non-streaming renders. In streaming SSR, hashes registered after the head has been sent cannot be added to its CSP <meta> tag. A warning for those calls could be added in a follow-up.

Docs

No documentation changes are needed. The docs already describe using Astro.csp inside components.

Changes

Adds .tif as an accepted image extension, next to .tiff. Tools like Lightroom and darktable export TIFFs as .tif, so those files currently have to be renamed before Astro treats them as images.

VALID_SUPPORTED_FORMATS is unchanged. It's checked against the detected format, which is still 'tiff', so image services see no difference.

fix(build): preserve mtime of public/ files and cached fonts
withastro/astro
#18503Oct 24

astro build was resetting the last-modified date on two classes of output files.

Root cause 1, public/ directory. Vite copies the public directory internally and does not forward mtime or atime. Every copied file ends up with the build timestamp rather than the source timestamp.

Root cause 2, Font files. The font plugin wrote fonts from an in-memory Buffer via writeFileSync, which always creates a fresh file with the current timestamp. The disk cache already held the font with the correct source mtime, but it was never consulted at write time.

What changed.

  • packages/astro/src/core/fs/index.ts: Added copyTimestamps(srcDir, destDir). It walks srcDir recursively and for each file calls fs.promises.utimes(destFile, atime, mtime) to copy the timestamp from the source tree. Files missing in destDir (e.g. files filtered by Vite) are silently skipped via ENOENT handling.

  • packages/astro/src/core/build/static-build.ts: After the client bundle build, calls copyTimestamps(settings.config.publicDir, outDir) to restore source timestamps on all public/ files.

  • packages/astro/src/assets/fonts/vite-plugin-fonts.ts: Changed font copying to call fontFetcher.fetch() (which populates the disk cache), then copyCachedFile(cacheFile, destFile) instead of writeFileSync(destFile, data). copyCachedFile already calls utimes after copying, so the cache mtime is preserved end-to-end. Dropped the unused writeFileSync import.

Verified. Logic confirmed by code review. The copyTimestamps helper mirrors the existing copyCachedFile pattern already used in the image pipeline. The font-path change has the same observable behavior since fontFetcher.fetch() always caches before returning.

Fixes #18483

Catch network errors in server island fetch to prevent uncaught TypeError
withastro/astro
#18497Oct 23

Changes

  • Failed fetch() calls in the generated server island client script no longer surface as Uncaught (in promise) TypeError. Previously, when a fetch rejected (network drop, aborted navigation, blocked cross-origin redirect), the top-level await in the island module would throw unhandled, polluting error trackers even though the fallback content remained visible. Both the GET and POST island fetch calls now append .catch(() => {}), and replaceServerIsland returns early on a missing response or a failed r.text() read, keeping the fallback silently.
  • The return statement suggested in the issue cannot be used at module top-level; the .catch(() => {}) approach achieves the same effect without a syntax error.

feat(check): add diagnostic reporters for stdout and files
withastro/astro
#18490Oct 23

Changes

Add diagnostic reporters to astro check for terminal output, scripts, and CI artifacts. Following Biome's reporter flags, --reporter selects how diagnostics and the run summary are written. Reports go to stdout unless an adjacent --reporter-file selects a file.

# JSON on stdout
npx astro check --reporter=json

# SARIF file only
npx astro check --reporter=sarif --reporter-file=reports/astro.sarif

# Live terminal diagnostics and a SARIF file
npx astro check --reporter=default --reporter=sarif --reporter-file=reports/astro.sarif

Supported formats are default, json, sarif, junit, and checkstyle. Repeat reporter/file groups for multiple outputs; a file flag without an adjacent reporter selects default plain text. Existing commands without reporter flags keep their default output.

  • Route Astro startup, telemetry notification, and sync logs to stderr when there is no default stdout reporter. Suppress default diagnostics, summaries, and watch control sequences in structured output. Node and JSON logger handlers accept an explicit output stream.
  • Preserve diagnostic codes, source locations, severity filtering, and exit status. JSON uses a documented versioned structure; SARIF uses UTF-16 columns and encoded file URIs. Each JUnit report contains one test whose failure follows the full results and --minimumFailingSeverity.
  • Resolve file paths from the working directory, create missing parent directories, and overwrite after completed checks. Cancelled or superseded checks preserve the previous report; report files are excluded from watching. Structured watch stdout emits consecutive completed report documents.
  • Expose a reporters array in the JavaScript API, plus reporter/reporterFile for a single output. Include a minor changeset for @astrojs/check and a patch changeset for Astro's CLI integration.

Docs

I've updated package README and linked reporting guide cover formats, stdout/file routing, repeated flags, JSON structure, severity mappings, CLI/API usage, paths, watch mode, and failures. CLI help is generated from the options.

The website CLI reference needs the corresponding options documented before release.

Skip CSP hashes for empty external styles and scripts
withastro/astro
#18488Oct 22

Fixes #18487

When CSP meta tags are on, createResult hashed children for every head style and script. External stylesheets and module scripts are stored as { props: { href|src }, children: '' }, so every page got 'sha256-47DEQpj8HBSa+/TImW+5JCeuQeRkm5NMpJWZG3hSuFU=' (the SHA-256 of the empty string) in script-src and style-src.

A hash in those directives makes 'unsafe-inline' ignored, so a project that relied on it for inline styles or scripts would lose that without asking.

Only entries with actual inline content (and no href/src) are hashed now.

Fix DataCloneError when importing SVGs with parallelPrerender enabled
withastro/astro
#18476Oct 21

Changes

  • SVG imports are Astro component functions with image metadata attached. When experimental.parallelPrerender is on, the prerender worker sends collected static-image transforms to the main thread via postMessage, which uses structured cloning — functions cannot be cloned, causing a DataCloneError. resolveStaticImage() now detects when transform.src is a function (i.e. an SVG component) and replaces it with a plain-object copy of the metadata before recording the transform, making the value serializable without changing the data the image service receives.

Testing

  • Added a unit test in packages/astro/test/units/assets/static-images.test.ts covering the case where an SVG component function is passed as src, asserting that the recorded transform stores a plain object rather than the original function.

Docs

  • No docs update needed; this is a bug fix for an experimental feature with no API surface change.

  • cfPrismPlugin now checks the adapter's isTypeGenPhase flag before appending include: ['prismjs/components/prism-*.js'] to the SSR environment's optimizeDeps. Respect exact version argument in @astrojs/upgrade
withastro/astro
#18466Oct 20

Changes

  • @astrojs/upgrade [version] now pins packages to the requested exact version instead of silently falling back to latest. resolveTargetVersion() previously only checked the argument against npm dist-tags; an exact semver like 7.3.8 never matched, so the CLI always resolved to latest with no warning.
  • The fix consults the versions map already present in the npm metadata. If the argument is a published version of a package, that version is used with no ^. Packages that never published that version (e.g. @astrojs/* integrations with their own version schemes) still fall back to ^latest, preserving existing behaviour.

Testing

Stop including Astro core packages in optimizeDeps for the Cloudflare Node prerender environment
withastro/astro
#18465Oct 20

Changes

  • Fixes astro dev rendering prerendered pages through productionEnvironment (instead of the dev render environment) when a custom src/fetch.ts is used with @astrojs/cloudflare and prerenderEnvironment: "node". This caused pages with hoisted <script> tags or hydrated islands to be truncated with Unable to resolve [...] errors.
  • The Cloudflare adapter no longer adds Astro core packages (astro, astro/fetch, astro/app, etc.) to optimizeDeps.include for the Node prerender environment. Previously those entries caused Vite to bundle a separate copy of those modules in node_modules/.vite/deps_prerender, giving new FetchState(request) its own empty copy of the environments WeakMap and making it fall back to productionEnvironment. The workerd prerender environment retains its include list unchanged.

Testing

  • Adds a test in packages/integrations/cloudflare/test/typegen-phase.test.ts covering the case where prerenderEnvironment: "node" is combined with a custom src/fetch.ts, asserting that the dev server renders the full page without Unable to resolve errors.

Docs

  • No docs update needed; this is a dev-server rendering correctness fix with no change to public API or configuration options.

Fix astro-check binary silently dropping the first two CLI arguments
withastro/astro
#18455Oct 20

Changes

  • bin/astro-check.js was passing process.argv.slice(2) to parseArgsAsCheckConfig(), which already calls yargs' hideBin() internally — stripping two more entries. This caused the first two user-supplied arguments to be silently ignored (e.g. astro-check --help ran diagnostics instead of printing help, and astro-check --root src ignored --root). The binary now passes the full process.argv, matching how parseArgsAsCheckConfig() is documented and how the astro check CLI caller works.
  • The packages/astro build script used astro-check -- -- --tsconfig ... as a padding workaround to compensate for the double-strip. That padding is removed now that the binary handles argv correctly; users with the same workaround in their own scripts should drop it too (noted in the changeset).

Testing

  • Added packages/language-tools/astro-check/test/bin.test.ts, which spawns the built binary with --help and asserts it exits successfully and prints help output. This test fails without the fix and passes with it.

Docs

  • No docs update needed; this is a bug fix restoring already-documented behavior for --root, --watch, --tsconfig, and --help.

Keep the query string and hash of sidebar links when formatting paths
withastro/starlight
#4287Oct 19

Description

  • Closes #
  • Manual sidebar links such as { label: 'Tabs', link: '/guides/components/#tabs' } are run through formatPath(), which adds the trailing slash or .html extension to the end of the whole string. With trailingSlash: 'always' this produces /guides/components/#tabs/, and with build.format: 'file' it produces /guides/components/#tabs.html, so the link no longer targets the section.
  • formatPath() now splits off any ?query or #hash suffix, formats only the pathname as before, and appends the suffix back. Links without a query or hash are unchanged.

Add fetchpriority=high on Hero images
withastro/starlight
#4285Oct 19

Description

  • Closes #

Was pretty simple so went straight to PR. Let me know if you'd prefer an issue.

  • What does this PR change? Give us a brief description.

The PR adds fetchpriority=high to hero images, along with the loading=eager and decode=async that already exist.

Fetchpriority improves loading time of key resources on the page as discussed here: https://web.dev/articles/fetch-priority and hero images are most likely to be the LCP image so are exactly the types of resources that benefit from this.

Full disclosure I work on the Chrome team and maintain the above doc, but this is available in all modern browsers (caniuse, MDN). Happy to answer any questions on this feature (or anything else in web performance space).

Neither the existing loading not decode are configurable, nor are the documented (presumably cause they are not configureable?) so I followed that implementation here. Happy to make it configurable instead and/or document this (and the others) if you prefer.

  • Did you change something visual? A before/after screenshot can be helpful.

No. This merely provides a slight performance boost to Hero images.

Fix `astro sync` replacing a running dev server's optimized dependencies
withastro/astro
#18451Oct 19

Changes

  • astro sync (also run by astro check and astro build) creates a temporary Vite server with optimizeDeps: { noDiscovery: true }. Astro itself (dev toolbar deps) and integrations such as @astrojs/react and @astrojs/preact add optimizeDeps.include entries, so Vite still runs the dependency optimizer on that server. It wrote to the project's default Vite cache, node_modules/.vite, which is the cache a running astro dev reads from. The dev server's optimized dependencies were replaced with ones built by the temporary server, for example React's production jsx-dev-runtime where jsxDEV is undefined, and islands broke with _jsxDEV is not a function or Invalid hook call until the dev server was restarted with --force.
  • The temporary server now uses its own Vite cacheDir, <cacheDir>/vite-sync/ under Astro's cacheDir. It optimizes the same dependencies as before and plugins see the same config; only where the output is written changes.

Fixes #18449

Testing

  • Added a test to test/astro-sync.test.ts. It writes a placeholder node_modules/.vite/deps/_metadata.json (standing in for a running dev server's cache) into a fixture that no other test starts a dev server on, runs sync, and asserts the file is unchanged. Without the change in sync/index.ts it fails, because sync replaces the placeholder with its own optimizer metadata. With the change, pnpm -C packages/astro exec astro-scripts test "test/astro-sync.test.ts" passes 10/10.
  • Checked the same change against the reproduction from #18449 (astro 7.4.0 + @astrojs/react): with astro dev running, node_modules/.vite/deps is no longer modified by astro sync, astro check or astro build, and sync's output goes to node_modules/.astro/vite-sync/deps.

Docs

No docs change. There is no API or config change; the only visible effect is a vite-sync directory inside Astro's cacheDir.

fix(upgrade): respect package manager minimum release age
withastro/astro
#18435Oct 18

Changes

  • @astrojs/upgrade now reads the package manager's release age policy (npm min-release-age, pnpm minimum-release-age).
  • It installs the newest version old enough instead of always pinning the newest. Before, the install failed when the policy blocked the newest version.
  • If nothing newer than the installed version is allowed yet, the package is reported as up to date.
  • Dist-tags (e.g. beta) are respected. It never moves past the tag's version, and prereleases are only considered when the target is one.
  • Fetches the full package metadata once per package, and only when a policy is set.
  • Changeset included.

Known limitations / not in this PR

  • Yarn and Bun are not detected yet. They behave as before: the newest version is pinned, and the install fails with the generic "run manually" message if their policy blocks it.
  • pnpm's existing minimumReleaseAge error message in install.ts is unchanged. It remains as a fallback for cases where detection misses the policy. It matches on a plain MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE substring without checking the package manager name. That is pre-existing and left alone here; a ctx.packageManager.name === 'pnpm' guard would be a small follow-up.
  • Transitive dependencies are not checked. The package manager resolves their ranges against the policy itself, and dependencies of an old-enough version should also be old enough. Peer dependency mismatches between packages pinned to different versions are not handled and have not been tested.

Testing

Added unit tests in packages/upgrade/test/verify.test.ts:

  • resolveTargetVersion: newest version is kept when old enough, an older allowed version is picked when it isn't, dist-tags are not passed, the installed version is kept when nothing newer is allowed, and publish times are ignored with no policy.
  • getMinReleaseAge: npm days, pnpm minutes, unset or null values, a failing config command, and unsupported package managers.

Also checked manually with --dry-run against astro 7.3.0 in an npm and a pnpm project (screenshots above): no policy targets 7.4.0, a 30-day policy targets 7.3.3, and a 60-day policy reports up to date.

Docs

No docs needed. This only changes which version the upgrade tool picks when a release age policy is set, and the changeset covers it.

Fix hydration with sparse array props
withastro/astro
#18431Oct 16

Changes

Sparse array props prevent framework components from hydrating. For example, Array(2) serializes as {"items":[1,[null,null]]} when passed as { items: Array(2) }. The island decoder expects a tagged tuple for every entry and throws a TypeError on the bare null values.

Array.prototype.map skips missing entries. Visiting every entry with Array.from lets the existing serializer encode each hole as undefined, producing {"items":[1,[[0],[0]]]}. This uses the existing wire format and leaves the client script unchanged. It does not preserve the distinction between a hole and an explicit undefined property.

Testing

Both added regressions fail before the fix; all 27 serializer tests pass after rebuilding. The package build, typecheck, and changed-file lint and formatting checks pass.

The packed serializer and production island script were also exercised in a real browser. Leading, all-hole, and nested sparse arrays reach the hydration callback as undefined entries; the same cases throw before the fix. An explicit-undefined control passes both. The full dev-server and e2e suites were not run.

Docs

No documentation change is needed. Arrays are already supported as hydrated props, and this fixes their serialization without adding an API. An astro patch changeset describes the fix.

fix(content): compute UTF-8 width arithmetically in getChunkEnd
withastro/astro
#18430Oct 16

Changes

Fixes #18429.

  • getChunkEnd() in data-store-writer.ts called TextEncoder.encode() once per character of the serialized store, only to learn that character's UTF-8 byte width. With experimental.collectionStorage: "chunked" this ran over the whole store on every sync and was ~63s of an 89s content sync on a 44k-entry (~180 MB serialized) store (node --cpu-prof on astro sync).
  • The width is fully determined by the code point, so compute it arithmetically: < 0x80 → 1, < 0x800 → 2, < 0x10000 → 3, else 4. Lone surrogates fall in the 3-byte branch, which matches the U+FFFD (3 bytes) that TextEncoder substitutes for them, so the two agree on every input.
  • Output is byte-identical: endIndex and bytes are unchanged for every input, so existing part files keep their xxhash names and nothing is invalidated.
  • Drops the now-unused module-level ENCODER.

Real project (16.4k pages, warm cache): content sync 89s → 5.5s, full astro build 2:28 → 1:31. Standalone: 20 MB string, chunkString() 10.30s → 0.08s, identical parts.

Testing

  • Added two unit tests to chunk-string.test.ts: code points on each UTF-8 width boundary (U+007F/U+0080/U+07FF/U+0800/U+FFFF/U+10000) with an exact expected split, and lone surrogates (high, low, reversed) budgeted as 3 bytes.
  • Existing chunkString tests unchanged and pass.
  • Differential fuzz of the original vs. the arithmetic getChunkEnd on ~25M cases (ASCII, 2/3-byte BMP, boundary values, astral pairs, lone/reversed surrogates, U+FFFD, NUL; maxBytes 1–1000; arbitrary start offsets including mid-pair), comparing both return values and the full chunkString() split: 0 mismatches. Script and timing repro: https://gist.github.com/Abhirup-99/2adc2e813117342d215f1b998a4a461a
  • Verified on the real store that all 14 part files hash identically before and after.

Docs

No docs change: internal performance fix, no user-facing behaviour change.

fix(transitions): stop Back from leaving the site in Chrome and Edge on iOS
withastro/astro
#18408Oct 16

Changes

Fixes #18377

  • WebKit marks a history entry as created without user interaction when pushState runs without recent user activation, and apps built on WKWebView, including Chrome and Edge on iOS, hide those entries from the back button. In Chrome on iOS a tap only counts as activation while its event is being dispatched. The router calls pushState after it has fetched the new page, so every entry it adds is hidden and Back leaves the site.
  • When a navigation starts with transient activation (navigator.userActivation.isActive), the router pushes the history entry right away as a copy of the current one, then fills it in with replaceState once the new page is swapped in.
  • If the router hands the navigation to the browser for a full page load, it uses location.replace() so the entry doesn't stay behind as a duplicate. A navigation that interrupts a pending one reuses its entry, and Back or Forward drops it.
  • #15163 was closed because it relied on UA sniffing. This follows the approach suggested in the issue, which doesn't need any browser detection.

In every browser, pressing Back while a page is still loading now returns to the current page instead of the previous one, because the entry already exists by then. The workaround posted in the issue behaves the same way. I can handle that case in a follow-up if you think it's worth it.

Testing

  • Added e2e tests to view-transitions.test.ts:
    • the history entry is added while the click is handled (fails without this change)
    • a navigation that interrupts another one doesn't add an extra entry
    • a full page load doesn't leave an extra entry
  • The view transitions e2e suite passes locally on Chrome and Firefox.
  • Tested on an iPhone 12 Pro Max (iOS 26.6.2, Chrome 154.0.8037.55) with the view-transitions fixture: open /one in a new tab by typing the address, go to /two, then press Back. Without this change Back leaves the site, with it Back goes to /one.

withfix.mov

Fix virtual module imports when the project path contains an apostrophe
withastro/astro
#18401Oct 15

Changes

  • Fixes a dev server 500 when the project path contains an apostrophe and a session driver is set, as @astrojs/node does by default. Astro writes the resolved driver path into the generated virtual:astro:session-driver module inside single quotes, so a path like ~/arc's site/ ends the string early and Vite can't parse the module.
  • The cache provider, middleware and src/fetch.ts modules break the same way. In dev, src/fetch.ts is then ignored without an error.
  • These import paths now go through JSON.stringify(), as the content layer already does. Paths without special characters resolve to the same files.

Reproduction with Astro 7.4.0 and @astrojs/node 11.1.8:

npm create astro@latest "arc's site" -- --template minimal --install --no-git --yes
cd "arc's site"
npx astro add node --yes
npx astro dev

Opening / returns a 500 and logs:

Failed to parse source for import analysis because the content contains invalid JS syntax. If you are using JSX, make sure to name the file with the .jsx or .tsx extension.
  Stack trace:
    at \0virtual:astro:session-driver:1:208

With pnpm and an on-demand page, astro build fails at the same module.

Testing

  • New test/units/virtual-module-imports.test.ts loads each of the four modules with an apostrophe in the resolved path and checks that the generated imports point at it. Without the fix, each case fails with a parse error.

Docs

  • None: bug fix, no API change.
Skip server island manifest in CSS ensureModulesLoaded to fix late-discovery 500 in dev
withastro/astro
#18399Oct 15

Changes

  • In dev, a server:defer island that imports astro:actions or astro:config/server would 500 with Could not find server component name if its page wasn't the first island page loaded after the server started. ensureModulesLoaded() in the CSS plugin was walking into virtual:astro:server-island-manifest and re-fetching it on the server side before the module runner could, causing the runner to keep a stale island map that was missing the newly discovered island.
  • ensureModulesLoaded() now skips RESOLVED_SERVER_ISLAND_MANIFEST. The manifest contains no CSS, so CSS collection is unaffected. The non-cascading refresh introduced in #18166 is preserved.

Testing

  • Added a dev-server integration test in packages/astro/test/server-islands.test.ts using a new test/fixtures/server-islands/late-discovery fixture. The test cold-starts the dev server, requests an island-free page first, then requests a second page whose island imports astro:actions, and asserts a 200 response (previously 500).

Docs

  • No docs update needed; this is a dev-only bug fix with no user-facing API changes.

Closes #18387

Update to pnpm 12
withastro/starlight
#4276Oct 15

Description

This PR updates the monorepo to pnpm 12.11.2 (latest tag).

  • Use the devEngines field to manage both the pnpm and Node.js versions.
  • Use Node.js 24.18.0 by default locally and in CI (ci.yml still tests using the minimum Node.js major version supported by Astro).
  • Use pnpm/setup in workflows.
  • Fix the devcontainer which was already broken before this PR and would have been even more after it. I tested locally that everything works as expected using the devcontainers CLI and Docker.
  • Enable minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune which automatically prunes entries in minimumReleaseAgeExclude when running a resolving commands (pnpm install, pnpm update, etc.). Note that a specific version is pruned only when that version is no longer in the lockfile (this means that an entry no longer requiring to be in minimumReleaseAgeExclude but still used would not be pruned automatically).
fix(vue): coerce SlotString so Vue SSR does not concatenate slot HTML char by char
withastro/astro
#18398Oct 15

Changes

  • @astrojs/vue's StaticHtml now coerces the slot value with String(...) before passing it to innerHTML.
  • Astro hands slots as SlotString (a String object). Vue's SSR buffer treats non-primitives as nested buffers and builds the output one character at a time, which becomes costly for large slots (for example island markup).

Fixes #18392

Testing

  • Added packages/integrations/vue/test/static-html.test.ts: renders with a String object and with a primitive; empty value returns null.
  • Ran: pnpm exec astro-scripts test "test/static-html.test.ts" (Node 22.20.0) → 2/2 pass.
  • Ablation bench (30× render of an 8k String object): coerced ~10ms vs uncoerced ~19ms locally; larger payloads widen the gap.
  • Did not run the full @astrojs/vue fixture suite (needs a full astro package build on this machine).

Docs

No docs change — internal SSR performance fix; user-facing behavior is unchanged.

AI assistance disclosure

An AI coding agent (Grok Bot) drafted this change. I reviewed the diff, ran the tests above, and take responsibility for the PR.

fix(vercel): match a trailing slash in isr.exclude routes
withastro/astro
#18391Oct 15

Changes

  • isr.exclude entries are written to the Vercel config as exact routes with no trailing slash (/account becomes ^/account$), but the ISR routes accept one (^(/([^/]+?)/?)$).
  • So a request for an excluded path with a trailing slash (/account/) skips its exclusion. If a dynamic route like [slug].astro also matches it, the request goes to the ISR function, and the response is cached and served to every visitor until it expires. For a page that depends on cookies, one visitor's page can be shown to others.
  • This allows an optional trailing slash on exclusion routes, the same way the ISR routes do. The edge-middleware path uses the same list (isrExcludedRoutes), so it's fixed there too.

Seen on a live site: /projects was in isr.exclude. /projects returned x-vercel-cache: MISS, while /projects/ returned STALE and its links picked up x_astro_path from the ISR rewrite.

Testing

  • isr.test.ts: updated the expected exclusion routes, and added a test that /two/, /excluded/foo/, /excluded/foo/bar/, /api/ and /api/foo/ all reach _render before any ISR route. The fixture's [a]/[b] route matches /excluded/foo/, which reproduces the bug.
  • isr-edge-middleware.test.ts: updated the expected /live route, and added a check that the middleware sends /live/ to _render. /live overlaps the fixture's [slug] route.
  • Without the source change, these four tests fail. With it, the full @astrojs/vercel suite passes.

Docs

No docs change. This makes isr.exclude behave the way the docs already describe it.

Refactor `copyFile` operations to preserve accessed and modified timestamps
withastro/astro
#18386Oct 15

Refactor file system operations on cached build files to preserve accessed and modified timestamps during file copy on all systems. Previously, these timestamps would only be preserved on static builds on MacOS.

This allows for faster and leaner synchronization of cached assets (fonts, images, etc.), and is especially useful when propagating incremental builds with many cached files.

Changes

  • Preserves last access and modified timestamps when copying files whenever fs.promises.copyFile is called

Testing

All current tests pass.
Built astro package linked to local repository and used for build; cached assets now maintain their modified date.
Unsure how to build a new test for this case specifically.
Edit: test has been added confirming that built assets maintain their cached version's modified date

Docs

No changes to docs as this is purely a file system optimization

fix(node): log "Server listening" when the server is already listening
withastro/astro
#18382Oct 14

Fixes #18381

Changes

  • logListeningOn waited for the listening event without checking whether it had already fired. standalone() calls it only after app.getLogger() resolves. For an IP literal HOST no DNS lookup delays listen(), so on Node 26.12 the event fires first and the Server listening on … line is never logged.
  • It now skips the wait when server.listening is already true:
 export async function logListeningOn(logger, server, configuredHost) {
-  await new Promise((resolve) => server.once('listening', resolve));
+  if (!server.listening) {
+    await new Promise((resolve) => server.once('listening', resolve));
+  }
   …
  • Changeset: @astrojs/node patch.

Testing

Added test/units/log-listening-on.test.ts. It calls logListeningOn on a server that already listens on 127.0.0.1, which is exactly the state standalone mode reaches on Node 26.12. The test does not depend on the Node version: it fails on 26.11 too without the fix.

  • Before: logs when the server is already listening fails; logListeningOn never settles ('timed out' instead of 'logged').
  • After: passes, and the full @astrojs/node suite passes (194 passed, 2 skipped).

End to end with the reproduction from the issue (https://github.com//astro-node-listening-repro), patching the built entry.mjs:

Node HOST=127.0.0.1, before after
26.11.1 line logged line logged
26.12.0 no line, HTTP 200 line logged

Docs

No docs change: this restores the documented startup message and changes no option or behaviour users configure.

fix(dev): treat missing ps row as stale in lockfile process check
withastro/astro
#18376Oct 14

Fixes #18343

On Linux, process.kill(pid, 0) succeeds for thread-ids, but ps -p <tid> returns no matching row. isLockFileProcessAlive was returning true (alive) when processInfo was undefined because processInfo?.cmd === undefined evaluates to true — so the function treated a thread-id lockfile entry as a live server.

This caused astro dev to refuse to start and, if the user force-cleared the lock, potentially send SIGTERM to an unrelated process that had recycled the same pid.

Fix: guard with an explicit undefined check — if ps returns no row the pid is not a running process, so the lock is stale.

// before
return processInfo?.cmd === undefined || isAstroCommand(processInfo.cmd)

// after
if (processInfo === undefined) return false
return isAstroCommand(processInfo.cmd)

Update dependency @qwik.dev/partytown to ^0.15.0
withastro/astro
#18372Oct 14

This PR contains the following updates:

Package Change Age Confidence
@qwik.dev/partytown ^0.14.5 → ^0.15.0

Release Notes

QwikDev/partytown (@​qwik.dev/partytown)

v0.15.0

Compare Source

Minor Changes
  • ✨ mainElementProperties config: properties a worker script sets on DOM elements (such as a function an iframe's inline onload calls) are also set on the real element, a function as a main thread function calling back into the worker. (by @​Varixo in #​776)
Patch Changes

  • 🐞🩹 fetch(request) with a Request object keeps its method, headers, body and credentials instead of sending a GET to its URL (prebid's bid requests). (by @​Varixo in #​782)

  • 🐞🩹 postMessage on any iframe's window from the worker goes through its iframe element, also for about:blank frames the main thread has no partytown window for. (by @​Varixo in #​779)

  • 🐞🩹 href of <link> and <base> elements is read and set on the main thread again, so a stylesheet a worker script adds with link.href = url loads; the no-op href every node has (for scripts walking up the tree) hid it. (by @​Varixo in #​780)

  • 🐞🩹 scripts loaded on the main thread via loadScriptsOnMainThread now fire the load/error handlers registered on them in the worker (onload, onerror, addEventListener), so loaders that wait for them (e.g. gtag's Google Ads viewthroughconversion) complete (by @​thegauravthakur in #​771)

  • 🐞🩹 a worker message listener can reply through the MessagePorts sent with the message (event.ports[0].postMessage), e.g. an ad library answering its creative's channel. (by @​Varixo in #​781)

  • 🐞🩹 in a worker message listener, event.source of a message from one of the page's iframes is that iframe's window, so replies through event.source.postMessage reach it (e.g. a consent tool answering an ad's __tcfapi call). (by @​Varixo in #​779)

  • 🐞🩹 worker scripts can talk to a cross-origin iframe the browser loaded itself (no CORS): iframe.contentWindow.postMessage reaches the frame, and the frame's reply to event.source reaches the page's message listeners instead of stopping at the partytown sandbox (e.g. a consent tool's consent store). (by @​Varixo in #​779)

  • 🐞🩹 window properties whose class partytown does not emulate, such as caches and scheduler, return the worker's own object instead of throwing "Illegal constructor". (by @​Varixo in #​778)

  • 🐞🩹 worker nodes get only the members every Node has: elements no longer inherit Text members such as splitText, which made libraries that detect text nodes by it (preact) treat elements as text nodes. (by @​Varixo in #​777)

  • 🐞🩹 don't read partytown scripts before the window's environment has been sent to the worker. Scripts added during page load (e.g. by streaming SSR, picked up by the MutationObserver) or a ptupdate before load were sent to a worker with no environment for the window, failed, and were never run again (by @​thegauravthakur in #​767)

  • 🐞🩹 tabs that start Partytown in the same millisecond, e.g. waiting for the same service worker to activate, get different tab ids, so the service worker no longer sends one tab's requests to the other tab ("Error finding instance"). (by @​gioboa in #​783)

  • 🐞🩹 window.eval(code) in a partytown script runs the code in the window's scope, like the script itself, instead of the worker's global scope where window, document and the page's globals are not defined (ad libraries run downloaded tags this way). (by @​Varixo in #​774)

  • 🐞🩹 define CSS in the web worker: CSS.escape() runs in the worker, and every other member (CSS.supports(), CSS.registerProperty(), …) is forwarded to the main thread. Scripts like gtag that call CSS.escape() no longer throw (by @​thegauravthakur in #​773)

expressjs/express (express)

v5.3.0

Compare Source

=====

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #​4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #​7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #​7057 and #​7478, and @​cyphercodes in #​7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #​7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #​7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #​5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #​6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #​7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #​6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #​7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

  • Upgrade body-parser to ^2.3.0, which fixes CVE-2026-12590 (GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6): an invalid limit option value caused request body size enforcement to be silently disabled (fail-open), allowing a denial of service via arbitrarily large payloads. Invalid limit values now throw at parser initialization instead of being ignored - by @​Mayvis in #​7390

⚡ Performance

  • Avoid duplicate Content-Type header processing in res.send() when sending string responses without an explicit Content-Type header - by @​bjohansebas in #​6991

astro@7.4.0

Minor Changes

  • #17894 b7a1bd9 Thanks @Princesseuh! - Adds a new --timings flag to astro build to help you find what slows down your builds

    When a build takes longer than expected, it can be hard to tell whether the cause is an integration, a Markdown processor plugin, image processing, or even syntax highlighting. Add the --timings flag to your build command to print a summary once the build finishes:

    astro build --timings

    This is helpful to decide what to optimize first, or to compare build times before and after a change to your project.

  • #17830 a937b0d Thanks @florian-lefebvre! - Adds a new optional getFontProperties() callback to font providers

    Font providers can now expose the weights, styles, subsets and formats a font family actually has. Astro uses it when resolving your font configuration to warn about values a provider cannot serve, for example a weight a font family does not offer.

    All built-in providers implement it. If you maintain a custom font provider, implementing this callback is optional for now but it will be required in Astro 8:

    import type { FontProvider } from 'astro';

const provider: FontProvider = {
	name: 'my-provider',
	resolveFont: ({ familyName }) => {
		// ...
	},
	getFontProperties: ({ familyName }) => ({
		weights: ['400', '700'],
		styles: ['normal', 'italic'],
		subsets: ['latin'],
		formats: ['woff2'],
	}),
};

  • #17830 a937b0d Thanks @florian-lefebvre! - Adds a fetch() function to the font provider init() context

    This function requests a provider API, retrying transient failures and more. It lets providers that wrap a 3rd-party unifont provider pass the context to it directly:

    import type { FontProvider } from 'astro';
import type { InitializedProvider } from 'unifont';
import { acmeProvider } from '@acme/unifont-provider';

export function acmeFontProvider(): FontProvider {
	const provider = acmeProvider();
	let initializedProvider: InitializedProvider | undefined;
	return {
		name: provider._name,
		async init(context) {
			initializedProvider = await provider(context);
		},
		// ...
	};
}

  • #18015 0b30239 Thanks @florian-lefebvre! - Adds experimental.redirectPage, letting you provide your own src/pages/3xx.astro in place of the redirect page Astro generates in static builds.

    A static site has no server to send an HTTP Location header, so Astro generates a small HTML page with a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> tag for each redirect it builds:

    • Your redirects entries
    • Astro.redirect() calls in prerendered pages
    • i18n redirects

    That page's markup, wording, and refresh delay were fixed, so you could not brand or translate it.

    To enable this feature, add the experimental flag to your Astro config:

    // astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  experimental: {
    redirectPage: true,
  },
});

    Then create src/pages/3xx.astro. Astro renders it once per redirect, passing that redirect's details as props:

    ---
// src/pages/3xx.astro
import type { RedirectPageProps as Props } from 'astro';

const { from, to, status, delay } = Astro.props;
---

<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta http-equiv="refresh" content={`${delay};url=${to}`} />
    <meta name="robots" content="noindex" />
    <title>Redirecting…</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <p>This page has moved. <a href={to}>Continue to {to}</a>.</p>
  </body>
</html>

    Your page must render a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> tag pointing at to, because in a static build that tag is the redirect. Astro logs a warning during the build if it is missing.

    See the experimental redirect page documentation for more information.

  • #18265 910ee69 Thanks @astro-factory! - Adds a notFound() handler to astro/fetch and astro/hono that renders the custom 404 page when no route matches, including a prerendered 404.astro

    Add it before pages() in a custom worker or server entrypoint that does not run inside App.render, such as a Hono app used directly as a Cloudflare worker. Without it, pages() and middleware() return an empty 404 with an internal X-Astro-Error header for unmatched routes. astro() already includes this handling.

    import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { notFound, pages } from 'astro/hono';
import { cf } from '@astrojs/cloudflare/hono';

const app = new Hono();
app.use(cf());
app.use(notFound());
app.use(pages());
export default app;

  • #18177 7d814e5 Thanks @Princesseuh! - Adds support for separate build and runtime image services

    image.service now also accepts a build and a runtime service. The build service optimizes images on prerendered pages when you build your site, and is also used during development. The runtime service handles images on on-demand rendered pages and the image endpoint of your deployed site.

    The following example uses Sharp to optimize images on prerendered pages, and an image CDN for on-demand rendered pages:

    // astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  image: {
    service: {
      build: { entrypoint: 'astro/assets/services/sharp' },
      runtime: { entrypoint: 'my-image-cdn-service' },
    },
  },
});

    Changes for integration authors

    config.image.service keeps the shape the user configured it with. When a project sets build and runtime services, config.image.service.entrypoint and config.image.service.config are undefined.

    If your integration reads image.service, check for the runtime property to get the service you need:

    'astro:config:done': ({ config }) => {
  const { service } = config.image;
  const runtimeService = 'runtime' in service ? service.runtime : service;

  if (runtimeService.entrypoint === 'astro/assets/services/sharp') {
    // ...
  }
},

    Setting image.service with updateConfig() replaces the existing service instead of merging with it when the two use different shapes. For example, setting a single service in a project that uses build and runtime services replaces both.

  • #18277 2715958 Thanks @florian-lefebvre! - Increases the minimum Node.js version to 22.22.0

    The minimum supported Node.js version is now 22.22.0, the latest Node.js 22 release supported by StackBlitz. This change is in line with Astro's Node.js support policy.

  • #18313 71e2b24 Thanks @matthewp! - Allows integrations to control where Astro writes client, server, and prerender build output.

    Custom prerenderers can access the final output locations through the new outputDirectories context:

    setPrerenderer((defaultPrerenderer, { outputDirectories }) => {
  const { client, server, prerender } = outputDirectories

  return createPrerenderer({
    defaultPrerenderer,
    client,
    server,
    prerender,
  })
})

  • #18177 7d814e5 Thanks @Princesseuh! - Lets custom prerenderers report the images used on prerendered pages

    Astro now generates images on prerendered pages from the image information that a prerenderer's getStaticPaths() and render() return. If your prerenderer wraps Astro's default one, pass this information through:

    setPrerenderer((defaultPrerenderer) => ({
  name: 'my-prerenderer',
  async setup() {
    await defaultPrerenderer.setup?.();
  },
  async getStaticPaths() {
    const result = await defaultPrerenderer.getStaticPaths();
    const { paths, metadata } = Array.isArray(result) ? { paths: result } : result;
    return { paths: paths.filter(({ pathname }) => !pathname.startsWith('/drafts')), metadata };
  },
  render(request, options) {
    return defaultPrerenderer.render(request, options);
  },
  async teardown() {
    await defaultPrerenderer.teardown?.();
  },
}));

    Returning a plain array from getStaticPaths() or a plain Response from render() still works, but is deprecated: images used on those pages are not generated.

  • #17932 b905ff1 Thanks @Princesseuh! - Adds support for experimental parallel prerendering

    This experimental feature makes astro build render your static pages in parallel, using multiple CPU cores at once instead of one. On sites with many pages, this can significantly reduce build times, at the cost of higher memory usage.

    To enable this feature, add the experimental flag in your Astro config:

    // astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  experimental: {
    parallelPrerender: true,
  },
});

    By default, Astro uses all available CPU cores but one. Each additional worker increases the memory used by your build. If your build runs out of memory, or does not get faster, set workers to a lower number:

    // astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  experimental: {
    parallelPrerender: {
      workers: 4,
    },
  },
});

    Each worker renders as many pages at once as your build.concurrency setting allows.

    This feature has no effect when your adapter provides its own way of prerendering pages. Among official adapters, this only applies to @astrojs/cloudflare. Astro logs a warning during the build when the flag is ignored.

    For more information on enabling and using this feature in your project, see the experimental parallel prerendering docs.

Propagate eager rendering errors in glob() loader so builds fail on Markdown plugin errors
withastro/astro
#18353Oct 12

Changes

  • astro build now exits with a non-zero status when a remark/rehype plugin throws during the glob() loader's eager rendering path. Previously the error was logged via logger.error() but swallowed, allowing CI to treat a failed content render as a successful build.
  • The fix adds throw error after the logger.error() call in the syncData catch block in packages/astro/src/content/loaders/glob.ts, so the rejection propagates through the Promise.all chain and fails the build — consistent with the behavior already present when deferRender: true is used.

Testing

  • Added a unit test in packages/astro/test/units/content-layer/glob-loader.test.ts (propagates eager rendering errors so the build fails) that verifies the loader rejects when eager rendering throws, ensuring the build process receives the error.

Docs

  • No docs update needed; this is a bug fix restoring expected error-propagation behavior with no API surface change.

Closes #18054

Fix ClientRouter clashing with script onload and onerror attributes
withastro/astro
#18352Oct 12

Changes

  • After a client-side navigation, the router executes each new <script src> and waits for it by setting onload and onerror on the script, then copies the original attributes across. An onload or onerror attribute sets the same handler, so whichever comes second replaces the other.
    • src before onload: the page's handler replaces the router's, and astro:page-load never fires.
    • onload before src: the router's handler replaces the page's, and the page's handler never runs.
  • The router now uses addEventListener for load and error, so both run.

Testing

Added an e2e test to view-transitions.test.ts with one script in each attribute order. It checks that astro:page-load fires and both onload handlers run. It fails without the fix and passes with it in Chrome and Firefox.

Docs

No docs needed. Nothing user-facing changes apart from the fix.

Move prismjs to dependencies in @astrojs/cloudflare
withastro/astro
#18351Oct 12

Changes

  • prismjs is moved from devDependencies to dependencies in the Cloudflare adapter's package.json. vite-plugin-prism.ts imports prismjs/components.js at the top level, which means any consumer importing @astrojs/cloudflare needs prismjs to be resolvable. Previously this worked only because pnpm's default hoisting made the copy bundled with astro (via @astrojs/prism) visible to the adapter — with hoisting disabled (pnpm global virtual store or hoist=false), the import fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
  • Declaring prismjs as a direct dependency ensures it is always installed alongside the adapter regardless of the package manager's hoisting behaviour.

Testing

  • No automated test was added. Inside the monorepo prismjs is always resolvable via workspace hoisting, so a unit test would pass with or without the fix. The fix was verified end-to-end by packing the adapter as a tarball and importing it in a standalone project with hoist=false.

Docs

  • No docs update needed; this is an internal dependency declaration with no user-facing API change.

Closes #18319

#18350Oct 12

This PR contains the following updates:

Package Change Age Confidence
